audio.spectrogramOverlapHelp: Fraction each FFT frame overlaps the previous one — the frame-step control. Higher = smoother in time (more frames, slower); lower = coarser/faster.
audio.spectrogramImageScalingHelp: How the image is scaled when zoomed in past the analysis resolution. Smooth = bilinear (soft); Sharp = nearest-neighbour (crisp pixels, blocky).
audio.spectrogramHighZoomModeHelp: Above the zoom threshold, re-analyse for sharper time detail. Smaller window = better time resolution (worse frequency resolution); Reassignment = sharpened ridges. Triggers a re-analysis when the threshold is crossed.
audio.spectrogramHighZoomThresholdHelp: Zoom factor at which the high-zoom detail profile activates (×1 = whole clip).
audio.spectrogramHighZoomWindowHelp: FFT window size used by the 'Smaller window' mode above the threshold. Smaller = sharper in time, coarser in frequency.
audio.spectrogramFreqScaleHelp: How the frequency (vertical) axis is spaced. Logarithmic matches human pitch perception; Linear spaces Hz evenly. Mel/Bark/ERB are perceptual scales.
audio.spectrogramStartHzHelp: Lowest frequency shown on the vertical axis.
audio.spectrogramStopHzHelp: Highest frequency shown. 0 = Nyquist (half the sample rate).
audio.spectrogramIntensityScaleHelp: How magnitude maps to brightness. Logarithmic (dB) reveals quiet detail; linear/root scales compress less.
audio.spectrogramGainHelp: Overall brightness in dB (0 dB = neutral); positive brightens, negative darkens.
audio.spectrogramDynamicRangeHelp: Range in dB between the darkest and brightest values shown. Larger reveals more low-level detail.
audio.spectrogramLimitHelp: Upper dB limit (ceiling); values above map to the brightest color.
audio.spectrogramFrequencyGainHelp: High-frequency emphasis, in dB per decade of frequency. Brightens the high frequencies.
audio.spectrogramSaturationHelp: Color saturation of the Classic color scheme (no effect on Pink/Grayscale).
audio.spectrogramPaletteHelp: Color scheme used to draw the spectrogram.
audio.spectrogramAlgorithmHelp: What the analysis computes: Frequencies (magnitude), Phase, Unwrapped phase, Reassignment (sharper), or Pitch (EAC).
audio.spectrogramWindowHelp: FFT window size in samples. Larger = finer frequency resolution but coarser time resolution.
audio.spectrogramWinFuncHelp: Window function applied before the FFT; trades off frequency resolution vs spectral leakage. Hann is a good default.
audio.spectrogramZeroPadHelp: Zero-padding factor. Interpolates the spectrum for a smoother display (does not add real resolution).
audio.spectrogramHopHelp: Hop size in samples between successive FFT windows. Smaller = more time columns (denser, slower).
audio.spectrogramChannelModeHelp: How stereo channels are handled: Combined (mixed) or Separate (per-channel).
